# Multiplayer readiness audit

**Assessment type:** Best-effort static inspection
**Verdict:** Blocked before playtest
**Scan completeness:** Complete
**Scope:** `calvindongsteam/remix_of_2879611305751680_1795468582` (world 2879611305751680) at `arvr/assets/hsr_packages/worlds/3D_Template_V2`: `3D_Template_V2.hzproject`, the active scene `space.hstf`, all 18 `.hstf` templates, 194 TypeScript scripts (41,015 lines), 330 `.assetmeta` files, project docs and config; every search family in the readiness checks, classified site by site

## Summary

The project is configured as single-player: `playerSettings.avatarMax` is `1`, so no second player can join. That is the only blocker. Under it the code is already written for multiplayer: the player template is networked, health and animation state replicate from each character's owner, every authority gate classifies as sound (no Class B), and the three weapon prefabs are attainable. Before a playtest, raise the cap and add spawn points: the scene has one spawn point, so every player and bot lands on the same spot. Nothing here has been run with several players yet.

## Runtime playtest checklist

- [ ] Two players join — with the cap raised, a second player joins, both appear, and each sees the other move, jump and dodge-roll smoothly
- [ ] Separate spawn spots — players and bots spawn at different points rather than stacked on one spot
- [ ] Late join — a player joining after another has moved and taken damage sees that player's current pose and health
- [ ] Contested weapon — two players press interact on the same weapon at once; exactly one holds it and the other's grab is refused cleanly
- [ ] Holder leaves — a player leaves while holding a weapon; it drops in the world and someone else can pick it up
- [ ] Defeated player — a player whose health reaches zero gets whatever you chose (respawn, revive or spectate) while the others keep playing
- [ ] Leave and rejoin — a player disconnects and rejoins with no duplicate character, camera or controls
- [ ] Bots fill — with bot fill on and its target at or below the cap, bots join to the target and leave as humans arrive
- [ ] Full room — at the maximum player count, frame time and movement stay smooth

## Unanalyzed

None

## Limitations

- This assessment is a best-effort static inspection, not runtime readiness certification.
- No atomic snapshot or project revision was captured; the project may have changed during the scan.
- The scan read the template's serialized files in its source directory rather than a live editor session: the maximum player count came from `3D_Template_V2.hzproject` `playerSettings.avatarMax`, and scenes and templates from their `.hstf` files.
- Framework scripts outside the project directory were resolved as references, not audited line by line.
- No creator-project changes were made.
